note: Theory that is heard, not recited: tap the three roots on the staff and hear the chord on each, follow the chords in order, then in a new order and in a second key with the key chips. The why gives the learner the method (listen for the root moving), and one word, the number, names a chord everywhere in the text. Works for any instrument, or none.

exercise.title: The 1, 4 and 5 chords in G, by ear
exercise.focus: G major · roots G C D · 1-4-5-1 by ear · then in C
exercise.why: Each chord is built on one note of the scale, so once you hear the root move from 1 to 4 to 5, you can name the chord that is playing.

sections.text: The staff below, the five lines of music, shows G major: tap a note to hear it. Tap the three ringed notes, {{1}}, {{4}} and {{5}}. Then press G, C and D in the chord boxes under the staff: each chord is built on one of those notes.

Press Play below to start the band: G, C, D and back to G, one bar each. Call out 1, 4 or 5 as each chord arrives, with the chord boxes to help. Keep going until you hear a change coming before the box lights.

Press Play below to start the band: the same three chords in a new order. Look away from the screen and call out the number of each chord, then look back to check. Then tap C in the Key row below and do it again: the chords are new, the numbers sound the same.
